habitat: Widely cultivated in gardens and nurseries across India
ecological_importance: Fragrant flowers attract nocturnal and diurnal moths and butterflies. Berries serve as occasional food sources for small frugivorous birds.
threats: None significant due to global horticultural propagation.
field_identification_notes: Intensely glossy, dark green, leathery leaves with prominent parallel veins.
Large, waxy, pristine white flowers with an overwhelmingly sweet, rich fragrance.
ml_relevance: Extremely glossy, dark green opposite leaves and waxy white flowers.

ar_information.quick_identification: Glossy dark green leaves; large waxy white flowers with sweet fragrance; ribbed orange fruits.
ar_information.conservation_message: Least Concern / Widely Cultivated. The fruit has been used for centuries across Asia as a natural yellow-gold dye source for textiles and food.

vit_campus_relevance.location: Campus administrative gardens and faculty quarters
